correctness.rationale: Holdener--Holdener give that \(N\) is an odd square, \(q\) is its least prime factor, and any other prime \(r\) is at least \(q+1\). Assuming two-prime support, Euler-factor bounds force \(r<q+3+4/(q-2)\), leaving \(r=q+2\) except the \((3,7)\) case. When \(r=q+2\), the exact abundancy identity forces the two divisor sums to be pure powers of the opposite prime; modulo \(r\) this gives incompatible congruences differing by a factor four. For \((3,7)\), the order of 3 modulo 7 gives the contradiction. The verifier checks the cutoff, special order and a large finite regression grid.
